reason: A more directly and plausibly suppresses Cr–Zr interdiffusion by placing a discrete refractory barrier at the interface while retaining an elemental-Cr outer coating, and it provides a straightforward baseline comparison and falsification test. B tests more accident-relevant temperatures, but its central mechanism—a dense Al-rich oxide forming specifically at the buried Cr–Zr interface—is poorly supported and physically questionable, while the cited 10 at.% Al result concerns a chemically distinct multielement coating and a non-Al-rich oxide.
